description: Define your dev environment as code. For microservice apps on Kubernetes.

summary.one_liner: Tilt is a developer tool that automates the build-and-deploy loop for microservice apps running on Kubernetes, configured through a Tiltfile.
summary.what_it_does: Tilt watches source files, rebuilds container images, and updates a Kubernetes dev environment when code changes, similar to running docker build and kubectl apply in a loop. Running `tilt up` starts a complete dev environment that the README says is configured for a team. The behavior is defined in a Tiltfile, which has a searchable API reference. The README points to tutorials and best-practice guides for configuring services in HTML, NodeJS, Python, Go, Java, and C#. It also links to Tilt Extensions, a collection of community-shared Tiltfile snippets. Tilt sends anonymized usage data by default, which the README documents separately.
use_cases: develop microservices against a Kubernetes cluster
automatically rebuild and redeploy containers on code change
define a team dev environment as code
replace manual docker build and kubectl apply steps
set up local dev for multi-service apps
how_to_run: macOS/Linux: curl -fsSL (install script URL truncated in README) | bash
Windows: run the PowerShell install command given in the README (URL truncated)
Other install options (Homebrew, Scoop, Conda, asdf) are in the Installation Guide
notable: Tiltfile-based configuration that defines the dev environment as code
Watches files and rebuilds container images automatically
Extensions system for adding new Tiltfile functionality
Language-specific best-practice guides for HTML, NodeJS, Python, Go, Java, and C#
caveats: Requires a Kubernetes environment; the README is built around Kubernetes microservice apps
Install commands in the README are truncated, so exact URLs must be taken from the Installation Guide
Sends anonymized usage data by default
